summary:
## Core Concept: A Fierce, Bronze & Gold Medusa

This tutorial creates a high-fashion, fantasy Medusa look that is **fierce**, **feminine**, and **sparkly**. The core of the aesthetic is a rich, **bronze and gold** color palette combined with sharp, graphic lines and special effects textures.

## Base & Contouring Techniques

*   **Eyebrow Blocking**: The look starts by completely hiding the eyebrows using a **glue stick** and concealer to create a smooth canvas for the dramatic eye makeup.
*   **Dramatic Contouring**: Instead of a traditional contour, a **black eyeshadow** is used to sharply carve out the cheekbones, jawline, and forehead. This is embellished with serpent-like **stripes** on the forehead for a more reptilian feel.

## Signature Medusa Eye Makeup

*   **Eyeshadow**: Create a high, dramatic wing with **gold eyeshadow** that extends up and over the brow area. Define this shape by smoking out a **black shadow** directly underneath it.
*   **Graphic Eyeliner**: Use a sharp liquid liner to draw a unique, bird-like double wing on the top lash line and a rounded wing on the bottom. Keep the lines precise and sharp.
*   **Finishing Touches**: Apply **gold glitter** to the lid and inner corner, use **white eyeliner** in the waterline to make the eyes appear larger, and finish with dramatic, winged **feathered lashes**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Avoid using black liner in the waterline. A white or nude liner is crucial for keeping the eyes looking large and open, which contrasts beautifully with the dark, graphic liner.

## Special Effects: Snake Scales & Gold Leaf

*   **Scale Texture**: Create realistic, small scales on the forehead, neck, and shoulders. 
    > [!TIP]
    > For a fine scale texture, rip a piece off a household **scrubby sponge**. Press water-activated paint through the sponge onto the skin. This method provides a more detailed result than using fishnet stockings.
*   **Gold Leaf**: Add a touch of royalty and texture by applying small, torn pieces of **gold leaf** under the graphic eyeliner and near the start of the eyebrows.

## Lips, Body & Final Touches

*   **Ombré Lips**: Create a striking ombré effect with a **black lip liner** and **liquid lipstick**. Blend a pressed **gold eyeshadow** into the very center for a pop of light.
*   **Body Glow**: Use a bronze body lotion and powder highlighter all over the chest, shoulders, and any exposed skin to create a dewy, almost 'sweaty' glow that catches the light.
*   **Accessories**: The transformation is completed with key accessories:
    *   Yellow **cat-eye contacts**.
    *   A custom wig with added **dreadlock clip-ins**.
    *   A snake necklace and a **DIY snake headpiece** (made from spray-painted plastic snakes).

## Introduction to the Medusa Look

Hey beauties, welcome back to my channel for Halloween. Today I'm gonna show you guys how to get this Medusa look for Halloween. I love this look. It is so bronzy. I think it's so fierce. It's feminine, it's glittery, sparkly. I love everything about it and I've been dying to do this look.

This look could be like the long-lost sister of my hypnotic mermaid makeup tutorials. If you love mermaids and you love fantasy looks, I'm gonna link it below for you guys to check out. And if you are loving this look, be sure you like this video, subscribe for more, and share with all your friends. Now let's jump right into the look.

## Creating a Flawless Base & Blocking Brows

Alright, so the first step for our look is to block out the brows. I'm just using a glue stick to do this and I'm going to be brushing those hairs flat against my skin. And I just like to go over it with a glue stick after it's dried as well to give them extra, extra flat against my skin. I'm going to be using a primer first to prime my skin and my body, and then going over those brows with a concealer as usual.

For a foundation, I'm going to use something that's a little bit thinner than my skin tone because I want a more luminous look today. I'm just blending that all over my face and brows. To lock that in, I'm just gonna use some bronzer because I want a really bronzy look. I'm going to use this all over my face and on my body as well, just covering all those pale areas.

## Dramatic Gold and Black Eyeshadow

We're gonna start with the Morphe Brushes 35O Spice palette and I'm gonna use this gold to create this wing that's kind of like going up over the brow into the hairline. And I'm just really winging that out, making it really, really pronounced.

And right underneath that, I'm gonna go in with a black eyeshadow and I'm gonna wing that up in the same direction and then just smoke it out using a smaller brush. Then I'm just gonna add in a little bit more black to really intensify that line, make it really dark. And here, I'm taking whatever is left on my brush and using it to blend and I'm gonna bring that down my nose to contour a little bit.

For the lid, I'm just using a gold eyeshadow from that palette and sweeping it all over and up. And I'm taking a brown shadow from that palette and smoking underneath that black line right above the gold so it blends together really seamlessly and there's just a little bit of a blending.

## Graphic Liner and Gold Glitter

So for the liner, I wanted to do something that was really different, really sharp, very winged, lots of lines going all over the place. So I did a really sharp, kind of bird-looking wings on the top lash line. On the lower lash line, I went in and created kind of like a round wing under the eye that wings outward so it makes the eye look really big. And I went back in and sharpened up the inner corners of those wings.

Here I'm gonna be using the Ghost Sculpt from Makeup Revolution just to mattify that liner. I'm gonna be using the bdellium tools Second Collection SFX brushes today. I love these so much. I highly recommend them to you guys. And you even get this bag inside of it that you can store your brushes in. I've just been using these pretty much all Halloween and I am obsessed. I'm gonna be using one of their brushes here to apply some glitter glue and then go right over the top with some glitter from Violet Voss. This is a beautiful gold, I'm so obsessed. I applied it into that inner corner of the eye between those wings. And I went and I applied this also to the lid space because I thought it was so pretty and it would look really, really nice. It will make the look really pop, which I'm really glad I added it because I think it looks amazing. So pretty and glittery.

And for the waterline, I'm going to be using a white eyeliner just to line that out and keep the eyes looking really big. We don't want to put any black in that waterline for this look. And here I'm just applying some mascara and feathered lashes so I get that winged effect on the eyes. You want this to be really, really dramatic and so you could really see that graphic liner.

## Intense Contouring and Gold Leaf

Here I'm just gonna be using an eyeshadow from Makeup Geek and this is a really beautiful gold color. I believe it's called Fortune Teller and I just, I love using this for bronzer looks. So I decided to use it all over my face. And here I'm just gonna hollow out the cheeks. I am using that Ghost Sculpt again and I'm going in and I'm kind of following the line of my cheekbone and going a little bit above it to get these really, really cut cheekbones, and it makes my face look really thin as well.

I'm gonna do the same thing in the inner corner area of the brow and then bring this up into the forehead. I was looking at pictures of snakes, and some snakes, especially cobras, they have a lot of stripes on them, so I wanted to add some stripes in my look. And I'm just using that same shade I contoured with to do this right now. And you can kind of blend this out using the fluffy brush.

I wanted to add some gold leaf to this look because I thought it was kind of royal and it looks really just beautiful with all this gold we got going on. So I thought I'd add in some gold leaf. So I applied it underneath that bottom line and I also added it right in the front of the brow area. And I wanted these to be small pieces so I could go in and cut them up first.

## How to Create a Scale Texture

I'm using a piece of a sponge right here actually to get the scales on my forehead. I had my mom hold this for me so I could get them really, really good. I'm using a water activated paint to press down into that sponge piece. So you could use fishnets, but if you want smaller scales, I would recommend just getting a scrubby sponge from the store and then ripping the piece off of it and doing what I did here, just pressing the paint in. I used very little water. I was really, really happy with the result.

## Achieving a Full-Body Bronze Glow

So I'm gonna be using this Backstage Glow from Victoria's Secret. I am obsessed with this lotion. I'm not 100% sure if they still call it Backstage Glow, but I will try to find something similar for you guys down below. They usually make these every year for the Fashion Show and they make you look so tan. Like if you're pale, I'm pretty pale, this literally makes you look so bronze, like you've been in the sun tanning for days or you've been to an island. I love it. So I had to use it for this look.

## Black and Gold Ombré Lips

I'm using a black lip liner for the lips. I'm gonna line them out and really pronounce that Cupid's bow. And this lip kit is from Makeup Revolution, and it comes with the liquid lipstick inside. So I'm gonna use that black liquid lipstick to fill in the rest of my lips, top and bottom. You want them to be really black.

We're gonna do an ombré lip today, so I'm gonna take that same gold shade that I used to blend all over my face for that golden glow. I'm gonna use this on the center of the lips. I'm just gonna tap this right into the center. I'm using that black shadow to really deepen up that ombré effect on the lips, and this is from the Ghost Sculpt palette.

## Applying Scales and Glitter to the Body

And going in with my bdellium tools brush, I'm gonna be using that golden eyeshadow we just used on the lips to bronze up that body. And I'm just kind of following my bone structure on my chest and also like around the halo of my body.

And here I'm using that scrubby sponge net again to add some more scales just to my shoulder. I didn't want this to overpower the look, so I just added a few more and I also added some to my neck and it really does look like snakeskin, which I love. I went over that with that gold shadow again. I used this shadow pretty much throughout the whole look. And then right in between those scales, I added some gold leaf.

I'm gonna be using my secret sauce right here. Yeah, it was a beautiful glitter. I'm gonna apply this all over the scales. I'm also going to add this pretty much all over my body, essentially. I just thought it needed tons of glitter, sparkle and shine. So I dabbed it into all the glittery areas under the eyes, the chest. You can see here how pretty it is against all that gold leaf and the scales. If you're going to a party, you definitely need to add some glitter to the body for sure. You can see me, I'm like loving this right now.

## Final Details, Contacts, and Accessories

I'm gonna apply my Halloween contacts here, pop those in. I went for some yellow ones. I'm gonna be using this eyeliner from EM Cosmetics. I'm just gonna add a little bit more darkness to this liner. I feel like it wasn't dark enough, so I really wanted it to be very black and I really like this liner because it's super sharp, so I really winged that out with it. And then I'm gonna add a little bit more of that glitter under the eyes. I can't just stop with the glitter man!

I'm gonna be using this Anastasia Beverly Hills Aurora highlighting palette. I'm gonna take that shade Eclipse and apply this basically all over my body. The key to this look is you want to kind of look sweaty, look kind of hot, you know what I mean? You want to look hot hot, like your actual temperature of your skin is hot. So I like lots of highlighter all over the body, bronzer, everything like that, you want to apply a lot of it.

And here I'm gonna be coating my fingertips in gold. I do this a lot; not essentially this color or black, but I decided to go with gold and then do the fingertips in black with some glitter dripping down. I'm gonna pop on my wig and my accessories. So this is like a snake necklace; popped that on. It went awesome with the look. And then my wig, I did add some dreadlock clip-ins to it that are brown just to kind of add a little spice to it and customize it a bit. And this headpiece I did make myself out of some plastic snakes, spray painted them and added glitter. If you guys want to know more about that, comment down below and I will be sure to answer you back.

## The Final Reveal and Outro

As you can see, this Medusa look is complete. And here's a look at the outfit. Yes, I couldn't help myself.

All right you guys, I hope you loved this Medusa look. I am so obsessed with this look, you have no idea. I've wanted this look for so long. So if you guys are loving it, be sure you comment down below, let me know what you think. Like this video if you did enjoy it, subscribe for more because we have more Halloween looks coming. And I will see you all in my next Halloween tutorial.
